title: 245. Functions, Graphs & Transformations: Determining Range from a Finite Mapping
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Range of a Finite Relation Given as Ordered Pairs
questions.learningObjective: Identify the range of a finite relation from its set of ordered pairs.
questions.question: For the relation \(R=\{(1,4),(2,5),(3,6)\}\), what is the range?
questions.explanation: The range of a relation is the set of all second coordinates, which are the output values. In \(R\), the second coordinates are \(4\), \(5\), and \(6\). Therefore the range is \(\{4,5,6\}\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: List the second coordinate in each ordered pair, then remove repeats.

questions.concept: Range from a Finite Mapping Diagram
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range from a finite mapping diagram.
questions.question: A mapping sends \(a\to2\), \(b\to3\), and \(c\to2\). What is the range?
questions.explanation: The range is the set of output values actually used by the mapping. The outputs are \(2\), \(3\), and \(2\). Listing each distinct output once gives \(\{2,3\}\). Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Collect all values on the output side of the mapping.

questions.concept: Range from a Table of Values
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range from a two-column table of values.
questions.question: A table shows \(x:1,2,3\) and \(y:7,8,8\). What is the range?
questions.explanation: In a table of values, the range is the set of \(y\)-values that appear. The \(y\)-values are \(7\), \(8\), and \(8\). After removing repeats, the range is \(\{7,8\}\). Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Use the output column and list each value only once.

questions.concept: Range of a Finite Mapping with Repeated Outputs
questions.learningObjective: Identify the range of a finite mapping when an output value repeats.
questions.question: A mapping is \(1\to5\), \(2\to5\), and \(3\to7\). What is the range?
questions.explanation: The outputs of the mapping are \(5\), \(5\), and \(7\). Repeating \(5\) does not add a new element to the range. The distinct outputs are \(5\) and \(7\), so the range is \(\{5,7\}\). Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: List the output values and count each distinct value only once.

questions.concept: Range from Ordered Pairs with Repeated Outputs
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of a finite relation when an output repeats.
questions.question: For the relation \(R=\{(a,1),(b,2),(c,3),(d,2)\}\), what is the range?
questions.explanation: The range is made up of the second coordinates of the ordered pairs. These are \(1\), \(2\), \(3\), and \(2\). After removing the repeated \(2\), the range is \(\{1,2,3\}\). Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Ignore the first coordinates and focus on the second coordinates.

questions.concept: Range versus Codomain in a Finite Mapping
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish the range from the codomain of a finite mapping.
questions.question: A mapping from \(X=\{1,2,3\}\) to \(Y=\{4,5,6,7\}\) is given by \(1\to4\), \(2\to5\), and \(3\to6\). What is the range?
questions.explanation: The codomain is the full set \(Y=\{4,5,6,7\}\), but the range is only the set of outputs actually assigned. The assigned outputs are \(4\), \(5\), and \(6\). Since \(7\) is not used, the range is \(\{4,5,6\}\). Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: The range contains only output values that are actually used by the mapping.

questions.concept: Range of a Finite Mapping That Is Not a Function
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of a finite mapping even when an input is repeated.
questions.question: A mapping is \(1\to2\), \(2\to3\), and \(1\to4\). What is the range?
questions.explanation: The range is determined only by the output values of the mapping, regardless of whether the relation is a function. The outputs are \(2\), \(3\), and \(4\). Therefore the range is \(\{2,3,4\}\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Look only at the output values, not at whether inputs repeat.

questions.concept: Range from a Table with Repeated Outputs
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range from a table when output values repeat.
questions.question: A table shows \(x:-1,0,1,2\) and \(y:3,3,5,5\). What is the range?
questions.explanation: The range is the set of \(y\)-values from the table. The \(y\)-values are \(3\), \(3\), \(5\), and \(5\). After removing repeats, the range is \(\{3,5\}\). Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Use the output row and eliminate repeated values.

questions.concept: Range of a Constant Finite Mapping
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range when all output values are the same.
questions.question: For the relation \(R=\{(-1,2),(0,2),(1,2)\}\), what is the range?
questions.explanation: Every ordered pair has second coordinate \(2\). Since the output is always \(2\), the only distinct output value is \(2\). Therefore the range is \(\{2\}\), so option A is correct.
questions.hint: List the second coordinate of each ordered pair, then keep each distinct value once.

questions.concept: Range from a Finite Mapping with Distinct Outputs
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of a finite mapping whose output values are all distinct.
questions.question: A mapping sends \(1\to2\), \(2\to4\), \(3\to6\), and \(4\to8\). What is the range?
questions.explanation: The range is the set of output values of the mapping. The outputs are \(2\), \(4\), \(6\), and \(8\). Since they are all distinct, the range is \(\{2,4,6,8\}\). Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: Collect all values on the output side and list them once each.
